title: Mall death ruled accidental
article: A coroner's jury has ruled the death of a Prince George man at a shopping mall last year was accidental.

After an inquest this week, the five-person panel concluded Darrell Raymond Paquette died of a combined overdose of cocaine and codeine, an ingredient found in Tylenol 3. No recommendations were made.

Unlike a criminal trial, an inquest doesn't lay blame for a death, but a jury may make recommendations on how to prevent future incidents. An inquest into Paquette's death was mandatory because he died while in police custody.

Paquette, 43, died Sept. 27, 2002 while being arrested for causing a disturbance at The Bay at Parkwood Place. The inquest heard he tumbled down the escalator while fleeing from store employees and struggled as staff and an off-duty police officer tried to restrain him. Efforts to revive him with CPR were unsuccessful.
Pathologist Dr. James McNaughton, who performed the autopsy, testified this week that Paquette died when a lethal dose of cocaine sent him into heart failure on the evening of Sept. 27, 2002.
A blood-alcohol level of .28 -- almost four times the legal driving limit -- and enough codeine to kill someone only made Paquette's condition worse, McNaughton testified.
